headline: Date Set: Vote to Remove Parliament's Speaker
script: Big one for democracy watchers: Parliament has set Wednesday, 26 August, for the vote on whether to remove Speaker Thoko Didiza. EFF leader Julius Malema tabled the motion back in June, angry that Didiza chose not to oppose President Ramaphosa's court bid to pause his own impeachment inquiry. Now there's a fresh fight: the vote's happening virtually, not in person, because parties agreed to cut back sittings so MPs can campaign for the local government elections. The EFF says you can't remove a Speaker over a video call, this needs a real sitting. Here's why it matters to you: this is about whether the people running Parliament's most powerful oversight processes, including holding a president accountable, are doing it fairly. How this vote goes could shape trust in the GNU heading into election season.
why_it_matters: It's a live test of whether Parliament can genuinely hold a sitting president accountable, something that shapes how much young voters can trust the system before they vote in November's local elections.

sources.title: Parliament sets date for debate on motion of no confidence in Speaker Thoko Didiza
